title: Lemon bars
subtitle: a crisp shortbread base with a set lemon curd topping
excerpt: Lemon bars are an American biscuit-bar with a crisp, buttery shortbread base and a firm, intensely lemony curd on top. The base is baked blind first, then the lemon filling is poured on and the whole thing goes back in the oven to set. They are dusted with icing sugar just before serving. The filling must use fresh lemon juice: bottled juice gives a flat flavour.
sourceNotes: Lemon bars are a classic American bar cookie, widely documented from the mid-twentieth century onward and well established in British home baking from the 1990s.

glossaryTerms.definition: Baking a pastry or biscuit base without its filling, to prevent the base becoming soggy once the wet filling is added.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze without the icing sugar dusting. Defrost at room temperature for 2 hours and dust with icing sugar just before serving.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make up to 2 days ahead and refrigerate. Dust with icing sugar just before serving.

content.text: Lemon bars bake in two stages: the shortbread base goes in first and is

until just set, then the lemon filling is poured on and the tin returns to the oven for a further 20 minutes. The filling is a lemon curd batter: eggs, sugar, lemon juice, and a little flour to set it. It should tremble slightly in the centre when removed from the oven; it will firm as it cools.

items.prepNote: zest of all 3 and juice (about 100 ml)

content.text: Heat the oven to 180°C fan. Line a 20 cm square tin with baking parchment, leaving a slight overhang.

Rub together the 150 g plain flour, 50 g icing sugar, and cold butter to fine crumbs. Press firmly and evenly into the base of the prepared tin. Bake for 15 to 18 minutes until pale golden. Remove from the oven but leave the oven on.
Whisk together the eggs, caster sugar, lemon zest, lemon juice, and 30 g plain flour until smooth. Pour immediately over the hot shortbread base.
Return to the oven and bake for 18 to 22 minutes until the filling is set at the edges but still has a slight wobble in the very centre. It will firm fully as it cools.
Leave to cool completely in the tin, then refrigerate for at least 2 hours before cutting. Lift out using the parchment overhang. Cut into 16 bars and dust generously with icing sugar.

attrs.problem: Filling is runny and does not set when cooled
attrs.avoid: Avoid removing from the oven while the centre is still completely liquid.
attrs.fix: Return to the oven for a further 5 minutes and check again; the edges should be fully set and the centre barely wobbly.

attrs.avoid: Avoid over-baking; once the edges are firm and the centre is set, remove immediately.
attrs.fix: A dusting of icing sugar hides any cracks. The texture is not affected.
